> **What this case shows** — during deep sleep the brain nests one rhythm inside
> another: the up-state of the **slow oscillation** (~1 Hz) gates the thalamocortical
> **sleep spindles** (~13 Hz), so spindle amplitude rises and falls with the
> slow-oscillation phase. This **slow-oscillation↔spindle coupling** is a hallmark of
> NREM sleep, implicated in memory consolidation. On a real overnight polysomnogram
> the Tort modulation index is **MI = 0.00035**, and it is unmistakably real: the
> observed coupling sits **z = 9.6** above a circular-shift surrogate null and exceeds
> **every one of 200 surrogates**. The ecosystem's `phaseAmplitudeCoupling` reproduces
> the canonical Python **tensorpac to machine precision** (|difference| = **5×10⁻¹⁷**)
> — fed the identical phase and amplitude, the two engines return the same modulation
> index to the last digit.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — to measure cross-frequency coupling: take the EEG → call
`phaseAmplitudeCoupling(x, sr, phase_band, amp_band, method="tort")` → read the
**modulation index** → test it against a **surrogate null** to confirm it is real.
**Way of thinking** — a phase-amplitude coupling is a *rhythm within a rhythm*; the
modulation index is only meaningful against a null that destroys the timing but keeps
the spectra (a circular shift), because band-limited signals produce a non-zero MI by
chance.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioCrossModal::phaseAmplitudeCoupling()` (Tort MI, Canolty
MVL, Ozkurt, PLV) and `eegComodulogram()` to scan a grid of phase × amplitude bands.
:::

## Proposition

On real NREM sleep EEG (Sleep-EDF SC4001, Fpz-Cz), the slow-oscillation phase
(0.5–1.25 Hz) and the spindle amplitude (12–15 Hz) are coupled: Tort MI = 0.00035,
z = 9.6 above a circular-shift null (exceeds all 200 surrogates), and
`phaseAmplitudeCoupling` equals the canonical `tensorpac` to machine precision.

## Question & goal

**The question is whether the ecosystem finds a genuine cross-frequency coupling, and
finds it the same way the field-standard tool does.** Cross-frequency coupling is
easy to over-claim — band-limited noise produces a non-zero modulation index. So the
goal is two-fold: (1) show the SO–spindle coupling is *real* against a proper
surrogate null, and (2) show the operator reproduces `tensorpac` exactly.

## Challenge & approach

A phase-amplitude coupling measure has two parts — extracting the phase and amplitude
(filter + Hilbert), then quantifying their relationship (the Tort modulation index).
We validate the *quantifier* by feeding the **identical** phase and amplitude to both
`phaseAmplitudeCoupling` and `tensorpac`, and we validate the *finding* by comparing
the observed MI to circular-shift surrogates.

```
NREM EEG → filter+Hilbert → SO phase, spindle amplitude ┐
                                                        ├─ Tort MI (== tensorpac)
                                                        └─ vs 200 circular-shift surrogates → z
```

## Data

**Sleep-EDF Expanded (sleep-edfx, PhysioNet)**: subject SC4001, overnight PSG. EEG
**Fpz-Cz** at 100 Hz; the first 30 min of concatenated **NREM (N2+N3)** epochs, grouped
from the dataset's own expert hypnogram (the same PSG the `netphys-sleep-network` case
reads). Details in [`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: normalized spindle amplitude across the slow-oscillation phase (two cycles shown) — spindle power is not flat but peaks at a preferred SO phase, the signature of coupling. Right: the observed Tort modulation index (red line) against the distribution of 200 circular-shift surrogates (grey) — the observation sits far into the tail (z = 9.6), above every surrogate.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* if there were no coupling, the left panel would be flat and the
red line on the right would fall inside the grey histogram. Instead the amplitude is
clearly modulated by phase, and the observed MI is nowhere near the null.

| Quantity | This reproduction | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| SO-spindle Tort MI | **0.00035** | `tensorpac` = 0.00035 |
| \|op − tensorpac\| | **5×10⁻¹⁷** | 0 (identical statistic) |
| Surrogate-null z | **9.6** | — |
| Surrogates exceeded | **200 / 200** | — |

The coupling is real and strong against the null, and the operator reproduces
`tensorpac` to machine precision. Values trace to
[`artifacts/pac_summary.csv`](artifacts/pac_summary.csv) and the phase–amplitude
distribution in
[`artifacts/pac_phase_distribution.csv`](artifacts/pac_phase_distribution.csv).

## Conclusion

The sleeping brain couples its slow oscillation to its spindles, and the ecosystem
measures that coupling with an operator that is exactly the field-standard `tensorpac`
— on real overnight EEG, confirmed real against a surrogate null. The transferable
takeaway: **report a coupling only when it beats a timing-destroying surrogate null,
and use a quantifier you have checked against the canonical tool — a non-zero
modulation index alone proves nothing.**

## Open questions

- The coupling was measured on one channel of one night. Its **preferred SO phase**
  (where spindles peak) and its strength are themselves biomarkers: tracking them
  across N2 vs N3, across the night, across subjects, and against a memory-task
  outcome would turn this validated PAC operator into a sleep/memory study; a
  **comodulogram** (`eegComodulogram`, a grid of phase × amplitude bands) would locate
  the coupling in frequency space rather than assuming the SO/spindle bands.
  *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| phase-amplitude coupling (Tort/Canolty/…) | `phaseAmplitudeCoupling()` | PhysioCrossModal |
| comodulogram (band grid) | `eegComodulogram()` | PhysioEEG |
| the aperiodic background (context) | `eegAperiodic()` | PhysioEEG |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **phase_band / amp_band** — pick the bands from the physiology (here SO 0.5–1.25 Hz,
  spindles 12–15 Hz); a comodulogram finds them when you do not know.
- **method** — `"tort"` (a normalized KL modulation index, 0–1-ish) is the robust
  default; Canolty MVL is amplitude-scale-dependent.
- **surrogates** — always test the MI against a timing-destroying null (circular shift
  of the amplitude); the raw MI is not interpretable on its own.
- **Nyquist** — the amplitude band must sit below the Nyquist frequency (here 50 Hz).

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioCrossModal)

# x = a numeric EEG signal (or a PhysioExperiment channel), sr in Hz
pac <- phaseAmplitudeCoupling(x, sr = 100,
                              phase_band = c(0.5, 1.25),   # slow oscillation
                              amp_band   = c(12, 15),      # sleep spindle
                              method = "tort")
pac$pac    # 0.00035 — the Tort modulation index

# exact by construction: matches the canonical tensorpac on the same phase+amp
# (tensorpac.methods.modulation_index) to machine precision.
```
